probes.requirement: Filter bounds are block numbers or tags, never block hashes: a hash bound is rejected (-32602 recommended), as eth_getLogs range bounds are.
Filter bounds do not accept EIP-1898 block-hash objects, which Parity, Erigon and Nethermind accepted: the request is rejected (-32602 recommended).
A blockHash selects exactly that block: the result equals the numeric single-block filter, each record localized with the requested hash, never another block’s records.
Address matching applies to the hash-selected block as to the numeric single-block filter.
Recipient matching, including a reward matched by its author, applies to the hash-selected block as to the numeric single-block filter.
mode union applies to the hash-selected block as to the numeric single-block filter.
after and count page the hash-selected block’s records as they page the numeric single-block filter.
A page past the end of the hash-selected block is [], as for the numeric single-block filter; alone it cannot show which block was selected.
A known block without matching records returns [], not an error, as the numeric single-block filter does; alone it cannot show which block was selected.
The genesis hash selects the genesis block, which has no trace records: [].
A non-null blockHash with a non-null fromBlock or toBlock is rejected (-32602 recommended), never answered by either selector.
Null fromBlock and toBlock are omitted, so a blockHash with null bounds selects that block.
A null blockHash is omitted, so the numeric range applies.
An unknown hash is an error (-32001), never [] or another block’s records.
An unknown hash is an error even with count 0: the selector is validated before any count 0 shortcut, so [] does not pass.
A blockHash that is not a 32-byte hash is rejected (-32602 recommended).
blockHash takes a bare 32-byte hash, not an EIP-1898 object: it is rejected (-32602 recommended).
